So a lot of these pages might not be marked on our wiki as having unknown parameters. But specifically keeping this comment here in case of import, these parameters should be added to [[Template:infobox ancient site]] rather than deleted from this draft or article[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:02, 28 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=I hope this is not too annoying but this article is gonna be placed under [[:Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] and there is a decent chance these unknown parameters are ones[[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] I want added to the main template like burial chamber structure and burial goods. Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|zh|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} |name = Nishinomiya Kofun |image = [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, entrance.jpg|280px]]
Entrance to the stone chamber |Alias = Nishinomiya No. 1 Kofun |location = {{ill|Heguri|ja|平群町}}, {{ill|Ikoma District, Nara|lt=Ikoma District|ja|生駒郡}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}
(inside Heguri Central Park) |coordinates = {{Coord|34|37|21.67|N|135|42|7.70|E|region:JP_type:landmark_map_size:20000|display=inline,title}} |type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}} |area = Side length: 35.6 meters
Height: Over 7 meters (estimated restored height: 8 meters) |burial = Bilateral {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} (Iwayayama sub-style)
(contains a hollowed-out house-shaped stone coffin) |burial goods Found = {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} |Constructed = Mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |Burial = (Possibly) {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王}} |other_designation Designation = Nara Prefecture Designated other_designation "Nishinomiya Kofun" |map = Japan Nara |Icon = Square Kofun |map_dot_label = Nishinomiya Kofun |map_dot_label = Top }} [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Mound}}]] '''Nishinomiya Kofun''' (西宮古墳/にしのみやこふん) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Heguri|ja|平群町}}, {{ill|Ikoma District, Nara|lt=Ikoma District|ja|生駒郡}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}} structure and has been designated as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a {{ill|keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト}}Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王}}, the son of {{ill|Shōtoku Taishi|ja|聖徳太子}}. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was designated as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated other_designation]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber dimensions are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * Burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the former site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the {{ill|modern period|ja|近世}}. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the {{ill|Iwayayama Kofun|ja|岩屋山古墳}} (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to form a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト}} (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. Nishinomiya Kofun, genshitsu-2-2.jpg|Burial chamber (entrance direction) Nishinomiya Kofun, sendou-2-2.jpg|Passage (entrance direction) Nishinomiya Kofun, sendou-1-2.jpg|Passage (burial chamber Height: Over 7 meters (estimated restored height: 8 meters) |burial = Bilateral {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} (Iwayayama sub-style)
(contains a hollowed-out house-shaped stone coffin) |burial goods Found = {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} |Constructed = Mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |Burial = (Possibly) {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王}} |other_designation Designation = Nara Prefecture Designated other_designation "Nishinomiya Kofun" |map = Japan Nara |Icon = Square Kofun |map_dot_label = Nishinomiya Kofun |map_dot_label = Top }} [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Mound}}]] '''Nishinomiya Kofun''' (西宮古墳/にしのみやこふん) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Heguri|ja|平群町}}, {{ill|Ikoma District, Nara|lt=Ikoma District|ja|生駒郡}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}} structure and has been designated as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a {{ill|keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト}}Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王}}, the son of {{ill|Shōtoku Taishi|ja|聖徳太子}}. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was designated as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated other_designation]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber dimensions are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * Burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the former site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the {{ill|modern period|ja|近世}}. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the {{ill|Iwayayama Kofun|ja|岩屋山古墳}} (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to form a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト}} (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. So a lot of these pages might not be marked on our wiki as having unknown parameters. But specifically keeping this comment here in case of import, these parameters should be added to [[Template:infobox ancient site]] rather than deleted from this draft or article[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:02, 28 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=I hope this is not too annoying but this article is gonna be placed under [[:Category:Pages using infobox ancient site with unknown parameters]] and there is a decent chance these unknown parameters are ones[[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] I want added to the main template like burial chamber structure and burial goods. Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|zh|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} |name = Nishinomiya Kofun |image = [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, entrance.jpg|280px]]
Entrance to the stone chamber |alternate_name = Nishinomiya No. 1 Kofun |location = {{ill|Heguri|ja|平群町}}, {{ill|Ikoma District, Nara|lt=Ikoma District|ja|生駒郡}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}
(inside Heguri Central Park) |coordinates = {{Coord|34|37|21.67|N|135|42|7.70|E|region:JP_type:landmark_map_size:20000|display=inline,title}} |type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}} |area = Side length: 35.6 meters
Height: Over 7 meters (estimated restored height: 8 meters) |burial = Bilateral {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} (Iwayayama sub-style)
(contains a hollowed-out house-shaped stone coffin) |burial goods Found = {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} |Constructed = Mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |Burial = (Possibly) {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王}} |other_designation Designation = Nara Prefecture Designated other_designation "Nishinomiya Kofun" |map = Japan Nara |type = Square Kofun |map_dot_label = Nishinomiya Kofun |map_dot_label = Top }} [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Mound}}]] '''Nishinomiya Kofun''' (西宮古墳/にしのみやこふん) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Heguri|ja|平群町}}, {{ill|Ikoma District, Nara|lt=Ikoma District|ja|生駒郡}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}} structure and has been designated as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a {{ill|keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト}}Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王}}, the son of {{ill|Shōtoku Taishi|ja|聖徳太子}}. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was designated as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated other_designation]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber dimensions are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * Burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the former site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the {{ill|modern period|ja|近世}}. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the {{ill|Iwayayama Kofun|ja|岩屋山古墳}} (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to form a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト}} (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. (contains a hollowed-out house-shaped stone coffin) |burial goods Found = {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} |Constructed = Mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |Burial = (Possibly) {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王}} |other_designation Designation = Nara Prefecture Designated other_designation "Nishinomiya Kofun" |map = Japan Nara |type = Square Kofun |map_dot_label = Nishinomiya Kofun |map_dot_label = Top }} [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Mound}}]] '''Nishinomiya Kofun''' (西宮古墳/にしのみやこふん) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Heguri|ja|平群町}}, {{ill|Ikoma District, Nara|lt=Ikoma District|ja|生駒郡}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}} structure and has been designated as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a {{ill|keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト}}Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王}}, the son of {{ill|Shōtoku Taishi|ja|聖徳太子}}. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was designated as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated other_designation]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber dimensions are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * Burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the former site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the {{ill|modern period|ja|近世}}. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the {{ill|Iwayayama Kofun|ja|岩屋山古墳}} (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to form a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト}} (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. (contains a hollowed-out house-shaped stone coffin) |burial goods Found = {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} |Constructed = Mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |Burial = (Possibly) {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王}} |other_designation Designation = Nara Prefecture Designated other_designation "Nishinomiya Kofun" |map = Japan Nara |type = Square Kofun |map_dot_label = Nishinomiya Kofun |map_dot_label = Top }} [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Mound}}]] '''Nishinomiya Kofun''' (西宮古墳/にしのみやこふん) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Heguri|ja|平群町}}, {{ill|Ikoma District, Nara|lt=Ikoma District|ja|生駒郡}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}} structure and has been designation1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a {{ill|keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト}}Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王}}, the son of {{ill|Shōtoku Taishi|ja|聖徳太子}}. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was designation1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated other_designation]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber dimensions are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * Burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the former site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the {{ill|modern period|ja|近世}}. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the {{ill|Iwayayama Kofun|ja|岩屋山古墳}} (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to form a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト}} (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. (contains a hollowed-out house-shaped stone coffin) |burial goods Found = {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} |Constructed = Mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |Burial = (Possibly) {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王}} |other_designation Designation = Nara Prefecture Designated other_designation "Nishinomiya Kofun" |map = Japan Nara |type = Square Kofun |map_dot_label = Nishinomiya Kofun |map_dot_label = Top }} [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Mound}}]] '''Nishinomiya Kofun''' (西宮古墳/にしのみやこふん) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Heguri|ja|平群町}}, {{ill|Ikoma District, Nara|lt=Ikoma District|ja|生駒郡}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}} structure and has been designation1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a {{ill|keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト}}Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王}}, the son of {{ill|Shōtoku Taishi|ja|聖徳太子}}. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was designation1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated other_designation]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber area are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * Burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the former site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the {{ill|modern period|ja|近世}}. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the {{ill|Iwayayama Kofun|ja|岩屋山古墳}} (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to form a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト}} (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. (contains a hollowed-out house-shaped stone coffin) |burial goods = {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} |Constructed = Mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |Burial = (Possibly) {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王}} |other_designation = Nara Prefecture Designated other_designation "Nishinomiya Kofun" |map = Japan Nara |type = Square Kofun |map_dot_label = Nishinomiya Kofun |map_dot_label = Top }} [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Mound}}]] '''Nishinomiya Kofun''' (西宮古墳/にしのみやこふん) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Heguri|ja|平群町}}, {{ill|Ikoma District, Nara|lt=Ikoma District|ja|生駒郡}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}} structure and has been designation1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a {{ill|keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト}}Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王}}, the son of {{ill|Shōtoku Taishi|ja|聖徳太子}}. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was designation1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated other_designation]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber area are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * Burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the former site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the {{ill|modern period|ja|近世}}. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the {{ill|Iwayayama Kofun|ja|岩屋山古墳}} (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to form a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト}} (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. (contains a hollowed-out house-shaped stone coffin) |burial goods = {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} |Constructed = Mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |Burial = (Possibly) {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王}} |other_designation = Nara Prefecture Designated other_designation "Nishinomiya Kofun" |map = Japan Nara |type = Square Kofun |map_dot_label = Nishinomiya Kofun |map_dot_label = Top }} [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Mound}}]] '''Nishinomiya Kofun''' (西宮古墳/にしのみやこふん) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Heguri|ja|平群町}}, {{ill|Ikoma District, Nara|lt=Ikoma District|ja|生駒郡}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}} structure and has been designation1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a {{ill|keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト}}Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王}}, the son of {{ill|Shōtoku Taishi|ja|聖徳太子}}. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was designation1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated other_designation]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber area are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * Burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the former site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the {{ill|modern period|ja|近世}}. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the {{ill|Iwayayama Kofun|ja|岩屋山古墳}} (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to form a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト}} (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. (contains a hollowed-out house-shaped stone coffin) |burial goods = {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} |Constructed = Mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |Burial = (Possibly) {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王}} |other_other_designation = Nara Prefecture Designated other_other_designation "Nishinomiya Kofun" |map = Japan Nara |type = Square Kofun |map_dot_map_dot_label = Nishinomiya Kofun |map_dot_map_dot_label = Top }} [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Mound}}]] '''Nishinomiya Kofun''' (西宮古墳/にしのみやこふん) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Heguri|ja|平群町}}, {{ill|Ikoma District, Nara|lt=Ikoma District|ja|生駒郡}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}} structure and has been other_designation1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a {{ill|keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト}}Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王}}, the son of {{ill|Shōtoku Taishi|ja|聖徳太子}}. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was other_designation1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated other_other_designation]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber area are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * Burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the typeer site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the {{ill|modern period|ja|近世}}. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the {{ill|Iwayayama Kofun|ja|岩屋山古墳}} (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to type a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト}} (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. (contains a hollowed-out house-shaped stone coffin) |burial goods = {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} |Constructed = Mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |Burial = (Possibly) {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王}} |other_other_designation = Nara Prefecture Designated other_other_designation "Nishinomiya Kofun" |map = Japan Nara |type = Square Kofun |map_dot_map_dot_label = Nishinomiya Kofun |map_dot_map_dot_label = Top }} [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Mound}}]] '''Nishinomiya Kofun''' (西宮古墳/にしのみやこふん) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Heguri|ja|平群町}}, {{ill|Ikoma District, Nara|lt=Ikoma District|ja|生駒郡}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}} structure and has been other_designation1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a {{ill|keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト}}Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王}}, the son of {{ill|Shōtoku Taishi|ja|聖徳太子}}. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was other_designation1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated other_other_designation]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber area are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * Burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the typeer site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the {{ill|modern period|ja|近世}}. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the {{ill|Iwayayama Kofun|ja|岩屋山古墳}} (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to type a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト}} (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. Entrance to the stone chamber |alternate_name = Nishinomiya No. 1 Kofun |location = {{ill|Heguri|ja|平群町}}, {{ill|Ikoma District, Nara|lt=Ikoma District|ja|生駒郡}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}
(inside Heguri Central Park) |coordinates = {{Coord|34|37|21.67|N|135|42|7.70|E|region:JP_type:landmark_map_size:20000|display=inline,title}} |type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}} |area = Side length: 35.6 meters
Height: Over 7 meters (estimated restored height: 8 meters) |burial = Bilateral {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} (Iwayayama sub-style)
(contains a hollowed-out house-shaped stone coffin) |burial goods = {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} |Constructed = Mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |Burial = (Possibly) {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王}} |other_designation = Nara Prefecture Designated other_designation "Nishinomiya Kofun" |map = Japan Nara |type = Square Kofun |map_dot_label = Nishinomiya Kofun |map_dot_label = Top }} [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Mound}}]] '''Nishinomiya Kofun''' (西宮古墳/にしのみやこふん) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Heguri|ja|平群町}}, {{ill|Ikoma District, Nara|lt=Ikoma District|ja|生駒郡}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}} structure and has been other_designation1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a {{ill|keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト}}Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王}}, the son of {{ill|Shōtoku Taishi|ja|聖徳太子}}. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was other_designation1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated other_designation]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber area are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * Burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the typeer site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the {{ill|modern period|ja|近世}}. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the {{ill|Iwayayama Kofun|ja|岩屋山古墳}} (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to type a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト}} (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. (contains a hollowed-out house-shaped stone coffin) |burial goods = {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} |Constructed = Mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |Burial = (Possibly) {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王}} |other_designation = Nara Prefecture Designated other_designation "Nishinomiya Kofun" |map = Japan Nara |type = Square Kofun |map_dot_label = Nishinomiya Kofun |map_dot_label = Top }} [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Mound}}]] '''Nishinomiya Kofun''' (西宮古墳/にしのみやこふん) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Heguri|ja|平群町}}, {{ill|Ikoma District, Nara|lt=Ikoma District|ja|生駒郡}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}} structure and has been other_designation1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a {{ill|keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト}}Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王}}, the son of {{ill|Shōtoku Taishi|ja|聖徳太子}}. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was other_designation1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated other_designation]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber area are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * Burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the typeer site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the {{ill|modern period|ja|近世}}. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the {{ill|Iwayayama Kofun|ja|岩屋山古墳}} (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to type a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト}} (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|zh|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} |name = Nishinomiya Kofun |image = [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, entrance.jpg|280px]]
Entrance to the stone chamber |alternate_name = Nishinomiya No. 1 Kofun |location = {{ill|Heguri|ja|平群町}}, {{ill|Ikoma District, Nara|lt=Ikoma District|ja|生駒郡}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}
(inside Heguri Central Park) |coordinates = {{Coord|34|37|21.67|N|135|42|7.70|E|region:JP_type:landmark_map_size:20000|display=inline,title}} |type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}} |area = Side length: 35.6 meters
Height: Over 7 meters (estimated restored height: 8 meters) |burial = Bilateral {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} (Iwayayama sub-style)
(contains a hollowed-out house-shaped stone coffin) |burial goods = {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} |Constructed = Mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |Burial = (Possibly) {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王}} |other_designation = Nara Prefecture Designated other_designation "Nishinomiya Kofun" |map = Japan Nara |type = Square Kofun |map_dot_label = Nishinomiya Kofun |map_dot_label = Top }} [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Mound}}]] '''Nishinomiya Kofun''' (西宮古墳/にしのみやこふん) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Heguri|ja|平群町}}, {{ill|Ikoma District, Nara|lt=Ikoma District|ja|生駒郡}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}} structure and has been other_designation1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a {{ill|keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト}}Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王}}, the son of {{ill|Shōtoku Taishi|ja|聖徳太子}}. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was other_designation1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated other_designation]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber area are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * Burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the typeer site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the {{ill|modern period|ja|近世}}. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the {{ill|Iwayayama Kofun|ja|岩屋山古墳}} (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to type a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト}} (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|Overhead view of the stone chamber Nishinomiya Kofun, sekkan-2.jpg|House-shaped stone coffin body Nishinomiya Kofun, genshitsu-1-2.jpg|Burial chamber (back wall direction) Nishinomiya Kofun, genshitsu-2-2.jpg|Burial chamber (entrance direction) Nishinomiya Kofun, sendou-2-2.jpg|Passage (entrance direction) Nishinomiya Kofun, sendou-1-2.jpg|Passage (burial chamber (inside Heguri Central Park) |coordinates = {{Coord|34|37|21.67|N|135|42|7.70|E|region:JP_type:landmark_map_size:20000|display=inline,title}} |type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}} |area = Side length: 35.6 meters
Height: Over 7 meters (estimated restored height: 8 meters) |burial = Bilateral {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} (Iwayayama sub-style)
(contains a hollowed-out house-shaped stone coffin) |burial goods = {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} |Constructed = Mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} |burial = (Possibly) {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王}} |other_designation = Nara Prefecture Designated other_designation "Nishinomiya Kofun" |map = Japan Nara |type = Square Kofun |map_dot_label = Nishinomiya Kofun |map_dot_label = Top }} [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Mound}}]] '''Nishinomiya Kofun''' (西宮古墳/にしのみやこふん) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Heguri|ja|平群町}}, {{ill|Ikoma District, Nara|lt=Ikoma District|ja|生駒郡}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}} structure and has been other_designation1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a {{ill|keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}, with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト}}Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王}}, the son of {{ill|Shōtoku Taishi|ja|聖徳太子}}. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was other_designation1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated other_designation]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber area are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the typeer site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the {{ill|modern period|ja|近世}}. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the {{ill|Iwayayama Kofun|ja|岩屋山古墳}} (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to type a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト}} (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage)..
