(contains a hollowed-out house-shaped stone coffin) |burial goods = {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}} |Constructed = Mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀|12=draft}} |burial = (Possibly) {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王|12=draft}} |Historic Site = Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site "Nishinomiya Kofun" |map = Japan Nara |type = Square Kofun |map_dot_label = Nishinomiya Kofun |map_dot_label = Top }} [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Mound}}]] '''Nishinomiya Kofun''' (西宮古墳/にしのみやこふん) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Heguri|ja|平群町|12=draft}}, {{ill|Ikoma District, Nara|lt=Ikoma District|ja|生駒郡|12=draft}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県|12=draft}}. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=draft}} structure and has been Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a {{ill|keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}}, with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=draft}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト|12=draft}}Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}} bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀|12=draft}}, marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|12=draft}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王|12=draft}}, the son of {{ill|Shōtoku Taishi|ja|聖徳太子|12=draft}}. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber area are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the typeer site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the {{ill|modern period|ja|近世|12=draft}}. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the {{ill|Iwayayama Kofun|ja|岩屋山古墳|12=draft}} (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to type a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト|12=draft}} (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. (contains a hollowed-out house-shaped stone coffin) |burial goods = {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}} |Constructed = Mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀|12=draft}} |burial = (Possibly) {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王|12=draft}} |Historic Site = Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site "Nishinomiya Kofun" |map = Japan Nara |type = Square Kofun |map_dot_label = Nishinomiya Kofun |map_dot_label = Top }} [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Mound}}]] '''Nishinomiya Kofun''' (西宮古墳/にしのみやこふん) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Heguri|ja|平群町|12=draft}}, {{ill|Ikoma District, Nara|lt=Ikoma District|ja|生駒郡|12=draft}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県|12=draft}}. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=draft}} structure and has been Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a {{ill|keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}}, with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=draft}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト|12=draft}}Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}} bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀|12=draft}}, marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|12=draft}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王|12=draft}}, the son of {{ill|Shōtoku Taishi|ja|聖徳太子|12=draft}}. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber area are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the typeer site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the {{ill|modern period|ja|近世|12=draft}}. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the {{ill|Iwayayama Kofun|ja|岩屋山古墳|12=draft}} (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to type a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト|12=draft}} (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. (contains a hollowed-out house-shaped stone coffin) |burial goods = {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}} |Constructed = Mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀|12=draft}} |burial = (Possibly) {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王|12=draft}} |Historic Site = Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site "Nishinomiya Kofun" |map = Japan Nara |type = Square Kofun |map_dot_label = Nishinomiya Kofun |map_dot_label = Top }} [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Mound}}]] '''Nishinomiya Kofun''' (西宮古墳/にしのみやこふん) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Heguri|ja|平群町|12=draft}}, {{ill|Ikoma District, Nara|lt=Ikoma District|ja|生駒郡|12=draft}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県|12=draft}}. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=draft}} structure and has been Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a {{ill|keyhole-shaped Kofun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}}, with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=draft}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}} have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト|12=draft}}Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery|12=draft}} bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀|12=draft}}, marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|12=draft}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of {{ill|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|ja|山背大兄王|12=draft}}, the son of {{ill|Shōtoku Taishi|ja|聖徳太子|12=draft}}. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber area are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the typeer site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the {{ill|modern period|ja|近世|12=draft}}. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the {{ill|Iwayayama Kofun|ja|岩屋山古墳|12=draft}} (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to type a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered {{ill|hyaloclastite|ja|ハイアロクラスタイト|12=draft}} (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. （平群中央公園内） |緯度度 = 34|緯度分 = 37|緯度秒 = 21.67 |経度度 =135|経度分 = 42|経度秒 = 7.70 |ISO = JP-29 |形状 = [[方墳]] |規模 = 一辺35.6m
高さ7m以上（推定復元8m） |埋葬施設 = 両袖式[[横穴式石室]]（岩屋山亜式）
（内部に刳抜式家形石棺） |出土品 = [[須恵器]] |陪塚 = |築造時期 = [[7世紀]]中葉-後半 |被葬者 = （一説）[[山背大兄王]] |陵墓 = |史跡 = 奈良県指定史跡「西宮古墳」 |有形文化財 = |特記事項 = |地図 = Japan Nara |アイコン = 方墳 |ラベル = 西宮古墳 |ラベル位置 = top }} [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|墳丘}}]] '''西宮古墳'''（にしのみやこふん/にしみやこふん）は、[[奈良県]][[生駒郡]][[平群町]]西宮にある[[古墳]]。形状は[[方墳]]。奈良県指定史跡に指定されている。 == 概要 == 奈良県北西部、平群谷の廿日山丘陵の南側斜面に築造された古墳である。廿日山丘陵では最高所に[[前方後円墳]]の上山1号墳が所在し、最高所南西に[[横口式石槨]]を有する[[方墳]]の[[上山2号墳]]が、南裾に方墳の西宮古墳・西宮2号墳が分布する。古くより石室が開口し、数次の調査が実施されている。 墳形は方形で、一辺約35.6メートル・高さ約7.2メートル以上（南側）を測る（推定復元高さ約8メートル）{{Sfn|続日本古墳大辞典|2002}}史跡説明板。。墳丘は3段築成で、墳丘斜面は約35度の勾配を持つ{{Sfn|続日本古墳大辞典|2002}}。墳丘外表では全面に貼石が認められ、貼石の下には約40センチメートルの裏込め礫層が認められるが{{Sfn|続日本古墳大辞典|2002}}、[[埴輪]]は認められていない{{Sfn|奈良県の地名|1981}}。また墳丘周囲には周溝が巡らされ、東側周溝底にも貼石が認められる。埋葬施設は両袖式の[[横穴式石室]]で、南方向に開口する。巨石の切石を用いた整美な石室であり、内部には兵庫県加古川流域産の竜山石製竜山石は、かつて流紋岩質溶結凝灰岩とされてきたが、近年の調査によって流紋岩質成層ハイアロクラスタイト（水冷破砕岩）と判明している（[https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html 宝殿石（竜山石）]（兵庫県ホームページ）参照）。の刳抜式[[家形石棺]]を据える。副葬品は失われているが、調査において[[須恵器]]坏蓋・高坏が出土している。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]中葉-後半頃と推定される。平群谷では代表的な[[終末期古墳]]として注目される。被葬者は明らかでないが、古墳の規模・内容から[[聖徳太子|厩戸皇子]]（聖徳太子）の子の[[山背大兄王]]の墓とする説が挙げられており、南1キロメートルでは厩戸皇子の離宮と推測される西宮遺跡が知られる[[河上邦彦]]『飛鳥発掘物語』扶桑社、2004年、pp. 73-75。。 古墳域は[[1956年]]（[[昭和]]31年）に奈良県指定史跡に指定されている。 == 埋葬施設 == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|石室俯瞰図}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|石室展開図}}]] 埋葬施設としては、両袖式の[[横穴式石室]]が構築されており、南方向に開口する。石室の規模は次の通り。 * 石室全長：約14メートル * 玄室：長さ約3.6メートル、幅約1.8メートル、高さ約1.8メートル 石室は巨石の切石を用いた整美なもので、奥壁・側壁・天井石にはいずれも一枚石が使用される。石材は平群町越木塚（石床神社旧社地付近）で産出する[[花崗岩]]である。石材の目地には漆喰が認められるほか、石室の床面には[[近世]]期に礫石経が敷かれ、羨門の天井石には墳丘斜面に合わせた傾斜を加工する（[[岩屋山古墳]]（[[明日香村]]）に類例）{{Sfn|奈良県の地名|1981}}。石室の床面は墳丘2段目のテラス面に合わせ、羨門前は墓道として一段下げる{{Sfn|続日本古墳大辞典|2002}}。 石室内には兵庫県加古川流域産の竜山石製の刳抜式[[家形石棺]]を据えており、現在は棺身のみが遺存する。棺身は長さ2.24メートル・幅1.15メートル・高さ0.76メートルを測り、外面の上下には帯状の突帯が造り出されている[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html 西宮古墳]（平群町ホームページ）。。 {{日本の古墳 |名称 = 西宮古墳 |画像 = [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, entrance.jpg|280px]]
石室開口部 |別名 = 西宮1号墳 |所属 = |所在地 = [[奈良県]][[生駒郡]][[平群町]]西宮
（平群中央公園内） |緯度度 = 34|緯度分 = 37|緯度秒 = 21.67 |経度度 =135|経度分 = 42|経度秒 = 7.70 |ISO = JP-29 |形状 = [[方墳]] |規模 = 一辺35.6m
高さ7m以上（推定復元8m） |埋葬施設 = 両袖式[[横穴式石室]]（岩屋山亜式）
（内部に刳抜式家形石棺） |出土品 = [[須恵器]] |陪塚 = |築造時期 = [[7世紀]]中葉-後半 |被葬者 = （一説）[[山背大兄王]] |陵墓 = |史跡 = 奈良県指定史跡「西宮古墳」 |有形文化財 = |特記事項 = |地図 = Japan Nara |アイコン = 方墳 |ラベル = 西宮古墳 |ラベル位置 = top }} [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|墳丘}}]] '''西宮古墳'''（にしのみやこふん/にしみやこふん）は、[[奈良県]][[生駒郡]][[平群町]]西宮にある[[古墳]]。形状は[[方墳]]。奈良県指定史跡に指定されている。 == 概要 == 奈良県北西部、平群谷の廿日山丘陵の南側斜面に築造された古墳である。廿日山丘陵では最高所に[[前方後円墳]]の上山1号墳が所在し、最高所南西に[[横口式石槨]]を有する[[方墳]]の[[上山2号墳]]が、南裾に方墳の西宮古墳・西宮2号墳が分布する。古くより石室が開口し、数次の調査が実施されている。 墳形は方形で、一辺約35.6メートル・高さ約7.2メートル以上（南側）を測る（推定復元高さ約8メートル）{{Sfn|続日本古墳大辞典|2002}}史跡説明板。。墳丘は3段築成で、墳丘斜面は約35度の勾配を持つ{{Sfn|続日本古墳大辞典|2002}}。墳丘外表では全面に貼石が認められ、貼石の下には約40センチメートルの裏込め礫層が認められるが{{Sfn|続日本古墳大辞典|2002}}、[[埴輪]]は認められていない{{Sfn|奈良県の地名|1981}}。また墳丘周囲には周溝が巡らされ、東側周溝底にも貼石が認められる。埋葬施設は両袖式の[[横穴式石室]]で、南方向に開口する。巨石の切石を用いた整美な石室であり、内部には兵庫県加古川流域産の竜山石製竜山石は、かつて流紋岩質溶結凝灰岩とされてきたが、近年の調査によって流紋岩質成層ハイアロクラスタイト（水冷破砕岩）と判明している（[https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html 宝殿石（竜山石）]（兵庫県ホームページ）参照）。の刳抜式[[家形石棺]]を据える。副葬品は失われているが、調査において[[須恵器]]坏蓋・高坏が出土している。 築造時期は、[[古墳時代]][[終末期古墳|終末期]]の[[7世紀]]中葉-後半頃と推定される。平群谷では代表的な[[終末期古墳]]として注目される。被葬者は明らかでないが、古墳の規模・内容から[[聖徳太子|厩戸皇子]]（聖徳太子）の子の[[山背大兄王]]の墓とする説が挙げられており、南1キロメートルでは厩戸皇子の離宮と推測される西宮遺跡が知られる[[河上邦彦]]『飛鳥発掘物語』扶桑社、2004年、pp. 73-75。。 古墳域は[[1956年]]（[[昭和]]31年）に奈良県指定史跡に指定されている。 == 埋葬施設 == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|石室俯瞰図}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|石室展開図}}]] 埋葬施設としては、両袖式の[[横穴式石室]]が構築されており、南方向に開口する。石室の規模は次の通り。 * 石室全長：約14メートル * 玄室：長さ約3.6メートル、幅約1.8メートル、高さ約1.8メートル 石室は巨石の切石を用いた整美なもので、奥壁・側壁・天井石にはいずれも一枚石が使用される。石材は平群町越木塚（石床神社旧社地付近）で産出する[[花崗岩]]である。石材の目地には漆喰が認められるほか、石室の床面には[[近世]]期に礫石経が敷かれ、羨門の天井石には墳丘斜面に合わせた傾斜を加工する（[[岩屋山古墳]]（[[明日香村]]）に類例）{{Sfn|奈良県の地名|1981}}。石室の床面は墳丘2段目のテラス面に合わせ、羨門前は墓道として一段下げる{{Sfn|続日本古墳大辞典|2002}}。 石室内には兵庫県加古川流域産の竜山石製の刳抜式[[家形石棺]]を据えており、現在は棺身のみが遺存する。棺身は長さ2.24メートル・幅1.15メートル・高さ0.76メートルを測り、外面の上下には帯状の突帯が造り出されている[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html 西宮古墳]（平群町ホームページ）。。 Nishinomiya Kofun, sekkan-2.jpg|家形石棺の棺身 Nishinomiya Kofun, genshitsu-1-2.jpg|玄室（奥壁方向） Nishinomiya Kofun, genshitsu-2-2.jpg|玄室（開口部方向） Nishinomiya Kofun, sendou-2-2.jpg|羨道（開口部方向） Nishinomiya Kofun, sendou-1-2.jpg|羨道（玄室方向） == 文化財 == === 奈良県指定文化財 === * 史跡 ** 西宮古墳 - 1956年（昭和31年）8月7日指定{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf 奈良県指定文化財一覧]}}（奈良県ホームページ）。。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} Entrance to the stone chamber |alternate_name = Nishinomiya No. 1 Kofun |location = [[:en:Heguri, Nara|Heguri]], [[:en:Ikoma District, Nara|Ikoma District]], [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]]
(inside Heguri Central Park) |coordinates = {{Coord|34|37|21.67|N|135|42|7.70|E|region:JP_type:landmark_map_size:20000|display=inline,title}} |type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=}} |area = Side length: 35.6 meters
Height: Over 7 meters (estimated restored height: 8 meters) |burial = Bilateral {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/corridor-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} (Iwayayama sub-style)
(contains a hollowed-out house-shaped stone coffin) |burial goods = [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] |Constructed = Mid to late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] |burial = (Possibly) [[:en:Prince Yamashiro|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]] |Historic Site = Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site "Nishinomiya Kofun" |map = Japan Nara |type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=}} |map_dot_label = Nishinomiya Kofun |map_dot_label = Top }} [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Mound}}]] '''Nishinomiya Kofun''' (西宮古墳/にしのみやこふん) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in [[:en:Heguri, Nara|Heguri]], [[:en:Ikoma District, Nara|Ikoma District]], [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]]. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=}} structure and has been Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]], with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/side-opening stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]]Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late [[:en:7th century|7th century]], marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/final period kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of [[:en:Prince Yamashiro|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]], the son of [[:en:Prince Shōtoku|Shōtoku Taishi]]. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber area are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the typeer site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the [[:en:Early modern period|modern period]]. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the [[:en:Iwayayama Kofun|Iwayayama Kofun]] (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to type a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]] (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|Overhead view of the stone chamber Nishinomiya Kofun, sekkan-2.jpg|House-shaped stone coffin body Nishinomiya Kofun, genshitsu-1-2.jpg|burial chamber (back wall direction) Nishinomiya Kofun, genshitsu-2-2.jpg|burial chamber (entrance direction) Nishinomiya Kofun, sendou-2-2.jpg|Passage (entrance direction) Nishinomiya Kofun, sendou-1-2.jpg|Passage (burial chamber direction) == Historic Site == === Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site === * Historic Site ''' Nishinomiya Kofun - Height: Over 7 meters (estimated restored height: 8 meters) |burial = Bilateral {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/corridor-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} (Iwayayama sub-style)
(contains a hollowed-out house-shaped stone coffin) |burial goods = [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] |Constructed = Mid to late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] |burial = (Possibly) [[:en:Prince Yamashiro|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]] |Historic Site = Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site "Nishinomiya Kofun" |map = Japan Nara |type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=}} |map_dot_label = Nishinomiya Kofun |map_dot_label = Top }} [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Mound}}]] '''Nishinomiya Kofun''' (西宮古墳/にしのみやこふん) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in [[:en:Heguri, Nara|Heguri]], [[:en:Ikoma District, Nara|Ikoma District]], [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]]. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=}} structure and has been Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]], with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/side-opening stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]]Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late [[:en:7th century|7th century]], marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/final period kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of [[:en:Prince Yamashiro|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]], the son of [[:en:Prince Shōtoku|Shōtoku Taishi]]. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber area are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the typeer site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the [[:en:Early modern period|modern period]]. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the [[:en:Iwayayama Kofun|Iwayayama Kofun]] (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to type a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]] (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. (contains a hollowed-out house-shaped stone coffin) |burial goods = [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] |Constructed = Mid to late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] |burial = (Possibly) [[:en:Prince Yamashiro|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]] |Historic Site = Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site "Nishinomiya Kofun" |map = Japan Nara |type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=}} |map_dot_label = Nishinomiya Kofun |map_dot_label = Top }} [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Mound}}]] '''Nishinomiya Kofun''' (西宮古墳/にしのみやこふん) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in [[:en:Heguri, Nara|Heguri]], [[:en:Ikoma District, Nara|Ikoma District]], [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]]. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=}} structure and has been Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]], with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/side-opening stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]]Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late [[:en:7th century|7th century]], marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/final period kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of [[:en:Prince Yamashiro|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]], the son of [[:en:Prince Shōtoku|Shōtoku Taishi]]. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber area are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the typeer site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the [[:en:Early modern period|modern period]]. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the [[:en:Iwayayama Kofun|Iwayayama Kofun]] (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to type a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]] (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the [[:en:Early modern period|modern period]]. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the [[:en:Iwayayama Kofun|Iwayayama Kofun]] (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to type a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]] (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=}} structure and has been Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]], with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/side-opening stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}}, located to the southwest. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]]Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late [[:en:7th century|7th century]], marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/final period kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]] (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]]Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late [[:en:7th century|7th century]], marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/final period kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of [[:en:Prince Yamashiro|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]], the son of [[:en:Prince Shōtoku|Shōtoku Taishi]]. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber area are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the typeer site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the [[:en:Early modern period|modern period]]. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the [[:en:Iwayayama Kofun|Iwayayama Kofun]] (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to type a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]] (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]]Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late [[:en:7th century|7th century]], marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/final period kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of [[:en:Prince Yamashiro|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]], the son of [[:en:Prince Shōtoku|Shōtoku Taishi]]. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber area are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the typeer site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the [[:en:Early modern period|modern period]]. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the [[:en:Iwayayama Kofun|Iwayayama Kofun]] (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to type a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]] (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. (contains a hollowed-out house-shaped stone coffin) |burial goods = [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] |Constructed = Mid to late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] |burial = (Possibly) [[:en:Prince Yamashiro|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]] |Historic Site = Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site "Nishinomiya Kofun" |map = Japan Nara |type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} |map_dot_label = Nishinomiya Kofun |map_dot_label = Top }} [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Mound}}]] '''Nishinomiya Kofun''' (西宮古墳/にしのみやこふん) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in [[:en:Heguri, Nara|Heguri]], [[:en:Ikoma District, Nara|Ikoma District]], [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]]. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} structure and has been Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]], with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/side-opening stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]]Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late [[:en:7th century|7th century]], marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/final period kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of [[:en:Prince Yamashiro|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]], the son of [[:en:Prince Shōtoku|Shōtoku Taishi]]. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber area are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the typeer site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the [[:en:Early modern period|modern period]]. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the [[:en:Iwayayama Kofun|Iwayayama Kofun]] (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to type a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped stone coffin made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]] (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|Overhead view of the stone chamber Nishinomiya Kofun, sekkan-2.jpg|House-shaped stone coffin body Nishinomiya Kofun, genshitsu-1-2.jpg|burial chamber (back wall direction) Nishinomiya Kofun, genshitsu-2-2.jpg|burial chamber (entrance direction) Nishinomiya Kofun, sendou-2-2.jpg|Passage (entrance direction) Nishinomiya Kofun, sendou-1-2.jpg|Passage (burial chamber direction) == Historic Site == === Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site === * Historic Site ''' Nishinomiya Kofun - Designated on August 7, 1956. == References == {{Reflist}} == Sources == {{small|(References used for writing this article)}} * Historical site explanation board (Nara Prefecture Board of Education, installed in 1999) * {{Cite book|Japanese|editor=|author=|year=1981|chapter=Nishinomiya Kofun|title=[[Japanese Place name Encyclopedia]] 30: Nara Prefecture|publisher=[[Heibonsha]]|isbn=4582490301|ref={{Harvid|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}}} * {{Cite book|Japanese|editor=|author=Kanekatsu Inokuma|year=1989|chapter=Nishinomiya Kofun|title=[[Japanese Kofun Encyclopedia]]|publisher=[[Tōkyōdō Shuppan]]|isbn=4490102607|ref={{Harvid|西宮古墳（古墳）|1989}}}} * {{Cite book|Japanese|editor=|author=Kunihiko Kawakami|year=2002|chapter=Nishinomiya Kofun|title=[[Japanese Kofun Encyclopedia Continued]]|publisher=[[Tōkyōdō Shuppan]]|isbn=4490105991|ref={{Harvid|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}}} == Related Literature == {{small|(Additional references not used in this article)}} * {{Cite book|Japanese|editor=|author=|year=1995|chapter=|title=Preliminary Report on the Excavation of Nishinomiya Kofun in Heguri Town, Nara Prefecture|publisher=Heguri Town Board of Education|isbn=|ref=}} * {{Cite book|Japanese|editor=|author=|year=2007|chapter=Nishinomiya Kofun (4th survey)|title=Summary Report of Excavations in Heguri Town, 1999–2001 and 2005|publisher=Heguri Town Board of Education|isbn=|ref=}} == See Also == * [[:en:Prince Yamashiro|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]] * [[:en:Udozuka Kofun|Udozuka Kofun]] * {{ill|Tsuboriyama Kofun|lt=Tsuboriyama Kofun|lt=Tsubori-yama Kofun|ja|ツボリ山古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsubori-yama Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|Heguri Shrine|ja|平群神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heguri Shrine|qq=}} * {{ill|Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun|ja|上山2号墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun|qq=}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Nishinomiya Kofun}} * [http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun Designated by Nara Prefecture] - (contains a hollowed-out house-shaped Sarcophagus) |burial goods = [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] |Constructed = Mid to late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] |burial = (Possibly) [[:en:Prince Yamashiro|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]] |Historic Site = Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site "Nishinomiya Kofun" |map = Japan Nara |type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} |map_dot_label = Nishinomiya Kofun |map_dot_label = Top |architectural_styles = {{ill|square kofun|qid=Q11504353}} }} [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Mound}}]] '''Nishinomiya Kofun''' (西宮古墳/にしのみやこふん) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in [[:en:Heguri, Nara|Heguri]], [[:en:Ikoma District, Nara|Ikoma District]], [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]]. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} structure and has been Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]], with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/side-opening stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped Sarcophagus made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]]Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late [[:en:7th century|7th century]], marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/final period kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of [[:en:Prince Yamashiro|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]], the son of [[:en:Prince Shōtoku|Shōtoku Taishi]]. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber area are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the typeer site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the [[:en:Early modern period|modern period]]. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the [[:en:Iwayayama Kofun|Iwayayama Kofun]] (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to type a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped Sarcophagus made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]] (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. (contains a hollowed-out house-shaped Sarcophagus) |burial goods = [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] |Constructed = Mid to late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] |burial = (Possibly) [[:en:Prince Yamashiro|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]] |Historic Site = Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site "Nishinomiya Kofun" |map = Japan Nara |type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} |map_dot_label = Nishinomiya Kofun |map_dot_label = Top |architectural_styles = {{ill|square kofun|WD=Q11504353}} }} [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Mound}}]] '''Nishinomiya Kofun''' (西宮古墳/にしのみやこふん) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in [[:en:Heguri, Nara|Heguri]], [[:en:Ikoma District, Nara|Ikoma District]], [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]]. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} structure and has been Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]], with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/side-opening stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped Sarcophagus made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]]Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late [[:en:7th century|7th century]], marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/final period kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of [[:en:Prince Yamashiro|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]], the son of [[:en:Prince Shōtoku|Shōtoku Taishi]]. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber area are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the typeer site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the [[:en:Early modern period|modern period]]. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the [[:en:Iwayayama Kofun|Iwayayama Kofun]] (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to type a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped Sarcophagus made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]] (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} structure and has been Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]], with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/side-opening stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped Sarcophagus made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]]Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late [[:en:7th century|7th century]], marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/final period kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of [[:en:Prince Yamashiro|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]], the son of [[:en:Prince Shōtoku|Shōtoku Taishi]]. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to type a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The kofun is dated to the mid to late [[:en:7th century|7th century]], marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/final period kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of [[:en:Prince Yamashiro|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]], the son of [[:en:Prince Shōtoku|Shōtoku Taishi]]. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber area are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the typeer site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the [[:en:Early modern period|modern period]]. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the [[:en:Iwayayama Kofun|Iwayayama Kofun]] (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to type a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped Sarcophagus made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]] (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} structure and has been Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]], with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/side-opening stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}}, located to the southwest. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}.
