However, no [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped Sarcophagus made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]]Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late [[:en:7th century|7th century]], marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/final period kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of [[:en:Prince Yamashiro|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]], the son of [[:en:Prince Shōtoku|Shōtoku Taishi]]. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber area are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the typeer site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the [[:en:Early modern period|modern period]]. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the [[:en:Iwayayama Kofun|Iwayayama Kofun]] (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to type a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped Sarcophagus made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]] (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]], with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/side-opening stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped Sarcophagus made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]]Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late [[:en:7th century|7th century]], marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/final period kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of [[:en:Prince Yamashiro|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]], the son of [[:en:Prince Shōtoku|Shōtoku Taishi]]. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber area are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the typeer site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the [[:en:Early modern period|modern period]]. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the [[:en:Iwayayama Kofun|Iwayayama Kofun]] (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to type a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped Sarcophagus made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]] (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. (contains a hollowed-out house-shaped Sarcophagus) |burial goods = [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] |Constructed = Mid to late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] |burial = (Possibly) [[:en:Prince Yamashiro|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]] |Historic Site = Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site "Nishinomiya Kofun" |map = Japan Nara |type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} |map_dot_label = Nishinomiya Kofun |map_dot_label = Top |architectural_styles = {{ill|square kofun|WD=Q11504353}} }} [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Mound}}]] '''Nishinomiya Kofun''' (西宮古墳/にしのみやこふん) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in [[:en:Heguri, Nara|Heguri]], [[:en:Ikoma District, Nara|Ikoma District]], [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]]. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} structure and has been Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]], with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/side-opening stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped Sarcophagus made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]]Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late [[:en:7th century|7th century]], marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/final period kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of [[:en:Prince Yamashiro|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]], the son of [[:en:Prince Shōtoku|Shōtoku Taishi]]. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber area are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the typeer site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the [[:en:Early modern period|modern period]]. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the [[:en:Iwayayama Kofun|Iwayayama Kofun]] (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to type a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped Sarcophagus made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]] (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. (contains a hollowed-out house-shaped Sarcophagus) |burial goods = [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] |Constructed = Mid to late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] |burial = (Possibly) [[:en:Prince Yamashiro|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]] |Historic Site = Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site "Nishinomiya Kofun" |map = Japan Nara |type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} |map_dot_label = Nishinomiya Kofun |map_dot_label = Top |architectural_styles = {{ill|square kofun|WD=Q11504353}} }} [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Mound}}]] '''Nishinomiya Kofun''' (西宮古墳/にしのみやこふん) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in [[:en:Heguri, Nara|Heguri]], [[:en:Ikoma District, Nara|Ikoma District]], [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]]. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} structure and has been Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]], with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/side-opening stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped Sarcophagus made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]]Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late [[:en:7th century|7th century]], marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/final period kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of [[:en:Prince Yamashiro|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]], the son of [[:en:Prince Shōtoku|Shōtoku Taishi]]. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber area are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the typeer site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the [[:en:Early modern period|modern period]]. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the [[:en:Iwayayama Kofun|Iwayayama Kofun]] (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to type a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped Sarcophagus made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]] (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. (contains a hollowed-out house-shaped Sarcophagus) |burial goods = [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] |Constructed = Mid to late [[:en:7th century|7th century]] |burial = (Possibly) [[:en:Prince Yamashiro|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]] |Historic Site = Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site "Nishinomiya Kofun" |map = Japan Nara |type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} |map_dot_label = Nishinomiya Kofun |map_dot_label = Top |architectural_styles = {{ill|square kofun|WD=Q11504353}} }} [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Mound}}]] '''Nishinomiya Kofun''' (西宮古墳/にしのみやこふん) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in [[:en:Heguri, Nara|Heguri]], [[:en:Ikoma District, Nara|Ikoma District]], [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]]. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} structure and has been Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]], with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/side-opening stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped Sarcophagus made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]]Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late [[:en:7th century|7th century]], marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/final period kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of [[:en:Prince Yamashiro|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]], the son of [[:en:Prince Shōtoku|Shōtoku Taishi]]. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber area are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the typeer site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the [[:en:Early modern period|modern period]]. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the [[:en:Iwayayama Kofun|Iwayayama Kofun]] (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to type a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped Sarcophagus made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]] (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} structure and has been Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]], with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/side-opening stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped Sarcophagus made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]]Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late [[:en:7th century|7th century]], marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/final period kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of [[:en:Prince Yamashiro|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]], the son of [[:en:Prince Shōtoku|Shōtoku Taishi]]. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to type a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]], with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/side-opening stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}}, located to the southwest. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]], with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/side-opening stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]] have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped Sarcophagus made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]]Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late [[:en:7th century|7th century]], marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/final period kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of [[:en:Prince Yamashiro|Prince Yamashiro no Ōe]], the son of [[:en:Prince Shōtoku|Shōtoku Taishi]]. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber area are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the typeer site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the [[:en:Early modern period|modern period]]. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the [[:en:Iwayayama Kofun|Iwayayama Kofun]] (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to type a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped Sarcophagus made of layered [[:en:Hyaloclastite|hyaloclastite]] (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|Overhead view of the stone chamber Nishinomiya Kofun, sekkan-2.jpg|House-shaped Sarcophagus body Nishinomiya Kofun, genshitsu-1-2.jpg|burial chamber (back wall direction) Nishinomiya Kofun, genshitsu-2-2.jpg|burial chamber (entrance direction) Nishinomiya Kofun, sendou-2-2.jpg|Passage (entrance direction) Nishinomiya Kofun, sendou-1-2.jpg|Passage (burial chamber direction) == Historic Site == === Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site === * Historic Site ''' Nishinomiya Kofun - (contains a hollowed-out house-shaped Sarcophagus) |burial goods = {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}} |Constructed = Mid to late {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century}} |burial = (Possibly) {{ill|Prince Yamashiro|en|Prince Yamashiro|WD=Q3137695|lt=Prince Yamashiro no Ōe}} |Historic Site = Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site "Nishinomiya Kofun" |map = Japan Nara |type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} |map_dot_label = Nishinomiya Kofun |map_dot_label = Top |architectural_styles = {{ill|square kofun|WD=Q11504353}} }} [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Mound}}]] '''Nishinomiya Kofun''' (西宮古墳/にしのみやこふん) is a {{ill|Kofun|en|Kofun|WD=Q1141225|lt=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Heguri, Nara|en|Heguri, Nara|WD=Q1346790|lt=Heguri}}, {{ill|Ikoma District, Nara|en|Ikoma District, Nara|WD=Q971003|lt=Ikoma District}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture}}. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} structure and has been Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun}}, with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/side-opening stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa}} have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped Sarcophagus made of layered {{ill|Hyaloclastite|en|Hyaloclastite|WD=Q964204|lt=hyaloclastite}}Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}} bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century}}, marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/final period kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of {{ill|Prince Yamashiro|en|Prince Yamashiro|WD=Q3137695|lt=Prince Yamashiro no Ōe}}, the son of {{ill|Prince Shōtoku|en|Prince Shōtoku|WD=Q263972|lt=Shōtoku Taishi}}. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber area are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the typeer site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the {{ill|Early modern period|en|Early modern period|WD=Q5308718|lt=modern period}}. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the {{ill|Iwayayama Kofun|en|Iwayayama Kofun|WD=Q11474389|lt=Iwayayama Kofun}} (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to type a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped Sarcophagus made of layered {{ill|Hyaloclastite|en|Hyaloclastite|WD=Q964204|lt=hyaloclastite}} (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. Entrance to the stone chamber |alternate_name = Nishinomiya No. 1 Kofun |location = {{ill|Heguri, Nara|en|Heguri, Nara|WD=Q1346790|lt=Heguri}}, {{ill|Ikoma District, Nara|en|Ikoma District, Nara|WD=Q971003|lt=Ikoma District}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture}}
(inside Heguri Central Park) |coordinates = {{Coord|34.622686111111|N|135.70213888889|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} |type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} |area = Side length: 35.6 meters
Height: Over 7 meters (estimated restored height: 8 meters) |burial = Bilateral {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/corridor-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} (Iwayayama sub-style)
(contains a hollowed-out house-shaped Sarcophagus) |burial goods = {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}} |Constructed = Mid to late {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century}} |burial = (Possibly) {{ill|Prince Yamashiro|en|Prince Yamashiro|WD=Q3137695|lt=Prince Yamashiro no Ōe}} |Historic Site = Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site "Nishinomiya Kofun" |map = Japan Nara |type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} |map_dot_label = Nishinomiya Kofun |map_dot_label = Top |architectural_styles = {{ill|square kofun|WD=Q11504353}} }} [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Mound}}]] '''Nishinomiya Kofun''' (西宮古墳/にしのみやこふん) is a {{ill|Kofun|en|Kofun|WD=Q1141225|lt=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Heguri, Nara|en|Heguri, Nara|WD=Q1346790|lt=Heguri}}, {{ill|Ikoma District, Nara|en|Ikoma District, Nara|WD=Q971003|lt=Ikoma District}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture}}. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} structure and has been Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun}}, with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/side-opening stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa}} have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped Sarcophagus made of layered {{ill|Hyaloclastite|en|Hyaloclastite|WD=Q964204|lt=hyaloclastite}}Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}} bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century}}, marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/final period kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of {{ill|Prince Yamashiro|en|Prince Yamashiro|WD=Q3137695|lt=Prince Yamashiro no Ōe}}, the son of {{ill|Prince Shōtoku|en|Prince Shōtoku|WD=Q263972|lt=Shōtoku Taishi}}. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber area are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the typeer site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the {{ill|Early modern period|en|Early modern period|WD=Q5308718|lt=modern period}}. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the {{ill|Iwayayama Kofun|en|Iwayayama Kofun|WD=Q11474389|lt=Iwayayama Kofun}} (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to type a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped Sarcophagus made of layered {{ill|Hyaloclastite|en|Hyaloclastite|WD=Q964204|lt=hyaloclastite}} (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|Overhead view of the stone chamber Nishinomiya Kofun, sekkan-2.jpg|House-shaped Sarcophagus body Nishinomiya Kofun, genshitsu-1-2.jpg|burial chamber (back wall direction) Nishinomiya Kofun, genshitsu-2-2.jpg|burial chamber (entrance direction) Nishinomiya Kofun, sendou-2-2.jpg|Passage (entrance direction) Nishinomiya Kofun, sendou-1-2.jpg|Passage (burial chamber direction) == Historic Site == === Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site === * Historic Site ''' Nishinomiya Kofun - Designated on August 7, 1956. == References == {{Reflist}} == Sources == Entrance to the stone chamber |alternate_name = Nishinomiya No. 1 Kofun |location = {{ill|Heguri, Nara|en|Heguri, Nara|WD=Q1346790|lt=Heguri|1=Heguri, Nara}}, {{ill|Ikoma District, Nara|en|Ikoma District, Nara|WD=Q971003|lt=Ikoma District|1=Ikoma District, Nara}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture|1=Nara Prefecture}}
(inside Heguri Central Park) |coordinates = {{Coord|34.622686111111|N|135.70213888889|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} |type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} |area = Side length: 35.6 meters
Height: Over 7 meters (estimated restored height: 8 meters) |burial = Bilateral {{ill|corridor-style stone chamber|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/corridor-style stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} (Iwayayama sub-style)
(contains a hollowed-out house-shaped Sarcophagus) |burial goods = {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery|1=Sue pottery}} |Constructed = Mid to late {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century|1=7th century}} |burial = (Possibly) {{ill|Prince Yamashiro|en|Prince Yamashiro|WD=Q3137695|lt=Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|1=Prince Yamashiro}} |Historic Site = Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site "Nishinomiya Kofun" |map = Japan Nara |type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} |map_dot_label = Nishinomiya Kofun |map_dot_label = Top |architectural_styles = {{ill|square kofun|WD=Q11504353|1=Square Kofun}} }} [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Mound}}]] '''Nishinomiya Kofun''' (西宮古墳/にしのみやこふん) is a {{ill|Kofun|en|Kofun|WD=Q1141225|lt=Kofun|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Heguri, Nara|en|Heguri, Nara|WD=Q1346790|lt=Heguri|1=Heguri, Nara}}, {{ill|Ikoma District, Nara|en|Ikoma District, Nara|WD=Q971003|lt=Ikoma District|1=Ikoma District, Nara}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture|1=Nara Prefecture}}. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} structure and has been Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}}, with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/side-opening stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa|1=Haniwa}} have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped Sarcophagus made of layered {{ill|Hyaloclastite|en|Hyaloclastite|WD=Q964204|lt=hyaloclastite|1=Hyaloclastite}}Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery|1=Sue pottery}} bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century|1=7th century}}, marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/final period kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of {{ill|Prince Yamashiro|en|Prince Yamashiro|WD=Q3137695|lt=Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|1=Prince Yamashiro}}, the son of {{ill|Prince Shōtoku|en|Prince Shōtoku|WD=Q263972|lt=Shōtoku Taishi|1=Prince Shōtoku}}. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber area are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the typeer site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the {{ill|Early modern period|en|Early modern period|WD=Q5308718|lt=modern period|1=Early modern period}}. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the {{ill|Iwayayama Kofun|en|Iwayayama Kofun|WD=Q11474389|lt=Iwayayama Kofun|1=Iwayayama Kofun}} (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to type a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped Sarcophagus made of layered {{ill|Hyaloclastite|en|Hyaloclastite|WD=Q964204|lt=hyaloclastite|1=Hyaloclastite}} (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-B.jpg|Overhead view of the stone chamber Nishinomiya Kofun, sekkan-2.jpg|House-shaped Sarcophagus body Nishinomiya Kofun, genshitsu-1-2.jpg|burial chamber (back wall direction) Nishinomiya Kofun, genshitsu-2-2.jpg|burial chamber (entrance direction) Nishinomiya Kofun, sendou-2-2.jpg|Passage (entrance direction) Nishinomiya Kofun, sendou-1-2.jpg|Passage (burial chamber It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} structure and has been Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}}, with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/side-opening stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa|1=Haniwa}} have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped Sarcophagus made of layered {{ill|Hyaloclastite|en|Hyaloclastite|WD=Q964204|lt=hyaloclastite|1=Hyaloclastite}}Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery|1=Sue pottery}} bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century|1=7th century}}, marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/final period kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of {{ill|Prince Yamashiro|en|Prince Yamashiro|WD=Q3137695|lt=Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|1=Prince Yamashiro}}, the son of {{ill|Prince Shōtoku|en|Prince Shōtoku|WD=Q263972|lt=Shōtoku Taishi|1=Prince Shōtoku}}. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber area are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the typeer site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the {{ill|Early modern period|en|Early modern period|WD=Q5308718|lt=modern period|1=Early modern period}}. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the {{ill|Iwayayama Kofun|en|Iwayayama Kofun|WD=Q11474389|lt=Iwayayama Kofun|1=Iwayayama Kofun}} (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to type a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped Sarcophagus made of layered {{ill|Hyaloclastite|en|Hyaloclastite|WD=Q964204|lt=hyaloclastite|1=Hyaloclastite}} (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. (contains a hollowed-out house-shaped Sarcophagus) |burial goods = {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery|1=Sue pottery}} |Constructed = Mid to late {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century|1=7th century}} |burial = (Possibly) {{ill|Prince Yamashiro|en|Prince Yamashiro|WD=Q3137695|lt=Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|1=Prince Yamashiro}} |Historic Site = Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site "Nishinomiya Kofun" |map = Japan Nara |type = {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} |map_dot_label = Nishinomiya Kofun |map_dot_label = Top |architectural_styles = {{ill|square kofun|WD=Q11504353|1=Square Kofun}} }} [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, funkyu-1.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Mound}}]] '''Nishinomiya Kofun''' (西宮古墳/にしのみやこふん) is a {{ill|Kofun|en|Kofun|WD=Q1141225|lt=Kofun|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Heguri, Nara|en|Heguri, Nara|WD=Q1346790|lt=Heguri|1=Heguri, Nara}}, {{ill|Ikoma District, Nara|en|Ikoma District, Nara|WD=Q971003|lt=Ikoma District|1=Ikoma District, Nara}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture|1=Nara Prefecture}}. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} structure and has been Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}}, with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/side-opening stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa|1=Haniwa}} have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. Surrounding the mound is a moat, with stone cladding also found at the bottom of the eastern side of the moat. The burial facility is a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The well-crafted chamber, built using large cut stones, houses a hollowed-out, house-shaped Sarcophagus made of layered {{ill|Hyaloclastite|en|Hyaloclastite|WD=Q964204|lt=hyaloclastite|1=Hyaloclastite}}Hyōgo Prefecture Homepage, [https://web.pref.hyogo.lg.jp/sr09/jibasan/31.html Ryuuzan Stone (Takatsuyama Stone)]. (known as Ryuzan Stone), sourced from the Kakogawa River basin in Hyōgo Prefecture. While the grave goods have been lost, fragments of {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|WD=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery|1=Sue pottery}} bowls and stands have been excavated during surveys. The kofun is dated to the mid to late {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century|1=7th century}}, marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/final period kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. Nishinomiya Kofun is a representative example of such kofun in the Heguri Valley. Although the identity of the individual buried here is unclear, the size and construction suggest that it might be the tomb of {{ill|Prince Yamashiro|en|Prince Yamashiro|WD=Q3137695|lt=Prince Yamashiro no Ōe|1=Prince Yamashiro}}, the son of {{ill|Prince Shōtoku|en|Prince Shōtoku|WD=Q263972|lt=Shōtoku Taishi|1=Prince Shōtoku}}. Approximately 1 kilometer south of the kofun lies the Nishinomiya Site, believed to have been the detached palace of Shōtoku TaishiKunihiko Kawakami, "Asuka Excavation Stories," Fusosha, 2004, pp. 73–75.. The site was Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture in 1956{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiitiran.pdf List of Nara Prefecture Designated Historic Site]}} (Nara Prefecture Homepage).. == burial == [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-P.jpg|thumb|300px|right|{{center|Perspective view of the stone chamber}}]] [[File:Nishinomiya Kofun, 3D-N.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Unfolded view of the stone chamber}}]] The burial facility consists of a bilateral corridor-style stone chamber opening to the south. The chamber area are as follows: * Total length: approximately 14 meters * burial chamber: Length approximately 3.6 meters, width approximately 1.8 meters, height approximately 1.8 meters The chamber is meticulously crafted using large cut stones, with single slabs of granite from Heguri Town's Koshikizuka area (near the typeer site of Sekitoko Shrine) used for the back wall, side walls, and ceiling. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the {{ill|Early modern period|en|Early modern period|WD=Q5308718|lt=modern period|1=Early modern period}}. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the {{ill|Iwayayama Kofun|en|Iwayayama Kofun|WD=Q11474389|lt=Iwayayama Kofun|1=Iwayayama Kofun}} (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to type a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped Sarcophagus made of layered {{ill|Hyaloclastite|en|Hyaloclastite|WD=Q964204|lt=hyaloclastite|1=Hyaloclastite}} (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. The coffin measures 2.24 meters in length, 1.15 meters in width, and 0.76 meters in height, and features belt-shaped bands carved into its outer surface[http://www.town.heguri.nara.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/bunkazai04-28.html Nishinomiya Kofun] (Heguri Town Homepage).. The kofun is dated to the mid to late {{ill|7th century|en|7th century|WD=Q8089|lt=7th century|1=7th century}}, marking the {{ill|final period kofun|ja|終末期古墳|1=Late Kofun tumuli|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/final period kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Late Kofun tumuli|qq=}}. The seams between the stones are sealed with plaster, and the floor is covered with gravel during the {{ill|Early modern period|en|Early modern period|WD=Q5308718|lt=modern period|1=Early modern period}}. The ceiling stone of the passage was cut to match the slope of the mound, similar to the {{ill|Iwayayama Kofun|en|Iwayayama Kofun|WD=Q11474389|lt=Iwayayama Kofun|1=Iwayayama Kofun}} (Asuka Village){{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}. The floor of the chamber aligns with the terrace of the second tier of the mound, with the passage entrance lowered to type a pathway{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. Inside the chamber lies a hollowed-out, house-shaped Sarcophagus made of layered {{ill|Hyaloclastite|en|Hyaloclastite|WD=Q964204|lt=hyaloclastite|1=Hyaloclastite}} (Ryuzan Stone). Currently, only the coffin body remains. It has a {{ill|square Kofun|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} structure and has been Historic Site1 as a historical site by Nara Prefecture. == Overview == Nishinomiya Kofun is located on the southern slope of the Hatsukayama Hills in the northwestern part of Nara Prefecture, in the Heguri Valley. At the highest point of the Hatsukayama Hills lies Kamiyama No. 1 Kofun, a {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|en|Zenpō-kōen-fun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpō-kōen-fun|1=Zenpō-kōen-fun}}, with Kamiyama No. 2 Kofun, a square Kofun featuring a {{ill|side-opening stone chamber|ja|横口式石槨|1=Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/side-opening stone chamber|13=User:Immanuelle/Side-entrance Sarcophagus Chamber|qq=}}, located to the southwest. Nishinomiya Kofun and Nishinomiya No. 2 Kofun are situated at the southern foot of the hills. The stone chamber of Nishinomiya Kofun has been open since ancient times, and multiple investigations have been conducted. The kofun is square-shaped, measuring approximately 35.6 meters on each side with a height of over 7.2 meters (estimated restored height of about 8 meters){{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}Historical site explanation board.. The mound consists of three tiers with a slope of about 35 degrees{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. The surface of the mound is entirely covered with stone cladding, and a backing layer of gravel approximately 40 cm thick is found beneath the cladding{{Sfn|西宮古墳（続古墳）|2002}}. However, no {{ill|Haniwa|en|Haniwa|WD=Q849376|lt=haniwa|1=Haniwa}} have been discovered{{Sfn|西宮古墳（平凡社）|1981}}.
